frequency_question: What proportion of federal agency administrative de-recognition or major revocation proceedings initiated against an established accrediting body or equivalent regulated entity are fully concluded with a final order within 71 days?
membership_rule: Includes any formal federal administrative process aimed at revoking institutional or programmatic accrediting authority, where the timeline from formal initiation to final agency determination is tracked. Excludes voluntary relinquishments.

cases.name: ACICS Final Appeal and Re-review Cycle
ABA Targeted Review and Compliance Proceedings

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 3 named precedent markers; universe of rapid complete de-recognitions under 71 days is empirically zero due to statutory procedural minimums.
known_gaps: Exact duration tracking for every sub-regulatory warning phase varies, but formal statutory steps structurally exceed 71 days.
skeleton: Standard federal administrative rulemaking and due process cycle: Notice and comment periods (min 30-60 days by statute), advisory committee review meetings (scheduled quarterly), and secretary review window.
multiplier: Statutory minimum notice (30 days) + mandatory advisory committee review window (minimum 90 days between convening cycles) + administrative drafting and final decision window (30-60 days). Minimum physical duration for a legally compliant process = ~150 to 210 days.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act and Higher Education Act statutory timelines remain fixed unless legislative overhaul occurs.
